rationale: TraceDag is an in-memory DAG model in Jaeger UI. It aggregates trace spans by service and operation and computes diffs between two traces, which drive the trace graph and comparison views. It is client-side analysis logic with behaviour of its own (building and diffing), not telemetry emission, so it is a notable application component.

A tiny TypeScript type describing a UI state update payload (reframe anchor/shift) for the trace timeline view. It is an internal state-shape detail with no callers, below the granularity a maintainer would name as an architectural element.

Trivial getter returning a private field on the OtelTraceFacade data model. It is an accessor, below the granularity a maintainer would name as an architecture element. It manipulates trace data for display but does not itself emit telemetry or render UI.

A trivial boolean predicate inside the Google Analytics tracking initializer that checks environment flags and the GA ID. It is an implementation detail of the tracking module, not an architectural element. It only gates telemetry and does not itself emit any.

A Redux middleware that, when web analytics is enabled, intercepts dispatched actions and runs registered tracking hooks (here, the timeline viewer's). It is conditional usage-analytics instrumentation of application code paths, so it is best modelled as an APM instrumentation configuration. It is a notable but small wiring unit.

An imperative ref handle type for a virtualized ListView component, exposing scroll and position accessors. It is an implementation-level TypeScript typing detail of a UI widget, not an element in its own right; the ListView component itself would be the UX element. It has no callers and only minor local relevance.

DraggableManager is a reusable UI interaction utility that handles mouse/drag events on DOM elements. Several Jaeger UI components (span graph viewing layer, timeline header, vertical resizer) share it. It is best modelled as a UX action pattern: a shared drag interaction recipe. It is a notable internal unit rather than a core architectural element.
Trivial accessor wrapper on TraceDag that looks up a node and throws if it is missing. It is an implementation detail below architectural granularity, with no cross-cutting concern of its own.

Trivial accessor module returning build-time injected constants (environment, version string, GA debug flag). It contains no behaviour, contract or structure a maintainer would name as an architectural element, so it is boilerplate below model granularity.

Pure string-formatting helper that shortens CSS selectors for breadcrumb payloads in Google Analytics tracking. It is a trivial regex utility called only by formatBreadcrumbs and does no telemetry work itself, so it is not an architectural element.

An in-memory data-holder class in the Jaeger UI model that wraps OTel span attribute arrays with a lazy key index. It holds state and exposes only trivial accessors, so it is an application data object. It is a minor internal unit, and it displays trace data rather than emitting telemetry itself.

A TypeScript props interface for the DAGOptions React component. It is a typing contract that is local to one UI component, not an architectural element in its own right. At most it could be recorded as an attribute of the component's prop schema, so it is classified as boilerplate below modelling granularity.

Trivial getter on the OtelTraceFacade that delegates to the wrapped legacy trace's traceName. It is an accessor and an implementation detail with no behaviour of its own, so it falls below the granularity a maintainer would name as an architectural element.

A small pure helper inside the service-filter hook. It enforces rules that keep root services visible in a pruned set. It is a minor internal unit, so it is modelled at most as an application function of low significance. It implements no cross-cutting concern itself: no storage, no rendering.

Generic Redux utility module wrapping reducers to skip actions lacking payload/meta. A trivial higher-order helper with no domain behaviour; it sits below the granularity a maintainer would name as an architectural element.

Vite ambient type declaration augmenting ImportMetaEnv with one optional environment variable. This is build/typing boilerplate with no behaviour, callers or callees, and it sits below the granularity of an architecture element.

A small data-normalization helper used when uploading OTEL trace files in Jaeger UI. It reshapes span fields such as timestamps and attributes. This is a transformation detail inside the upload utility, not a modelled element. It handles telemetry data but does not itself emit or configure telemetry.

A client-side controller class that drives TracePage scrolling: it pages the view and jumps to the previous or next visible span. It is a behavioural unit with its own state, injected into TracePageImpl, but it is not itself a rendered view. It is a notable internal component of the trace viewer UI.

A generated-style API client method bound to GET /metrics/{type} on the Jaeger query backend, with Zod response validation. API client methods count as evidence for api operations. It is called from the Monitor view's metrics query and is a notable but not central endpoint consumer.

This module defines the span filter criteria model, its evaluation logic and the f= URL codec that the trace timeline consumes. It is notable client-side application logic implementing RFC 0009 filtering, not a UI view itself. It handles telemetry data in the Jaeger UI but emits no telemetry, so observability is false.

Global TypeScript declaration augmentation adding an optional Redux DevTools hook to the Window type. It is pure typing boilerplate supporting store configuration, with no behaviour or architectural meaning of its own.

A trivial predicate wrapper around parseContentEntries, used for GenAI attribute parsing in the span detail tab. It is an implementation detail below architectural granularity, with no callers and no cross-cutting work of its own.

Trivial immutable state toggle on a UI detail-state class that flips a boolean for whether the resource section is expanded. It is an implementation detail of span detail panel state, below the granularity of an architectural element.

Test fixture module providing a synthetic trace and expected critical path sections for critical-path algorithm tests. It is test data scaffolding, one of many numbered cases. No testing element type fits a raw fixture well, so the element type is null and significance is minor.

An adapter in Jaeger UI's in-memory model. It wraps a legacy Span and exposes it through the IOtelSpan interface, precomputing kind, attributes, events, links, status and resource. It carries trace data for display and does not emit telemetry, so it is an application data object and not an APM element. It is notable within the OTel model migration.

GraphModel is the core in-memory model for Jaeger UI's Deep Dependency Graph. It builds vertices and edges from path elements and computes visibility and generation logic. Because it owns substantive behaviour rather than just holding data, it is an application component. It is central to the DDG feature but performs no I/O, auth or rendering itself.

A trivial one-field TypeScript interface used as an update payload type for trace view time-range shifting. It is a small local type in the UI's internal state plumbing, below the granularity a maintainer would name as an architectural element.

Module containing only numeric layout-fraction constants for the trace timeline viewer. These are implementation details and configuration values, not an architectural element. Although they are UI-related, the module itself renders nothing.

A trivial setter on ScrollManager that assigns the trace field so the trace can be supplied after construction. It is an accessor and an implementation detail with no behaviour of its own, below the granularity an architecture model would record.

A UI utility that assigns stable palette colors to keys (e.g. service names in trace views) using an in-memory cache. It is a presentation helper below the granularity of an architecture element. It does no persistence, integration or rendering of its own, so no concerns apply.

A pure arithmetic helper that computes five evenly spaced Y-axis tick values for a chart component. It is a trivial formatting utility below architectural granularity, and it does not itself render UI or implement any cross-cutting concern.

Trivial ref-setter callback inside a React component that stores the SVG root element on the instance. It is an implementation detail of the ViewingLayer UI component and not an architectural element on its own.

A date and duration formatting utility module (dayjs wrappers, unit constants, percentage helpers). It is a generic formatting helper below architectural granularity. It neither renders UI itself nor emits telemetry, so it does not qualify as a modelled element.

A React component overlaying the trace minimap that renders the current view range and handles mouse drag interactions for reframing it. It is a reusable UI component with props, not a routable view, so it maps to a ux librarycomponent of moderate significance within the TracePage header.

A TypeScript type augmentation adding a dataLayer property to Window for Google Analytics typing. It is a trivial typing helper with no behaviour of its own. It supports GA tracking code but is not itself an architectural element.

A trivial Redux reducer case that resets the set of collapsed span IDs to an empty set. It is a small state-transformation helper inside the timeline duck module, below the granularity a maintainer would name as an architectural element. It does no persistence, rendering or telemetry itself.

A small arithmetic helper on the virtualized list's Positions class that extrapolates the total height from the average known row height. It is an internal layout computation, not an architectural element. It does not render UI itself.

A small React presentational component that renders a hover tooltip for flamegraph nodes, showing name, percentage, duration and span count. It is a UI component with a props contract, but it is a minor part of the TraceFlamegraph view, so its architectural significance is low.

A small lookup helper that maps a visibility index to a vertex key through in-memory graph maps. It has a single caller and no architectural role of its own; it is an implementation detail of getDerivedViewModifiers.

Tween is a small animation-interpolation utility (easing over requestAnimationFrame) used only by the scroll-page helpers. It is an implementation detail of smooth scrolling, not a view, component or transition template a maintainer would model. It drives values via callbacks but does not itself render UI.

IFlameNode is an in-code data structure that carries flamegraph tree data from the OTel trace converter to the UI component. It is neither persisted nor published as a schema, so it is an application data object of minor, file-local significance.

A small convenience method on GraphModel that composes two other methods to compute a visibility encoding with one vertex hidden. It is an internal helper of the DDG graph model, below the granularity a maintainer would name as an architectural element.

A small React hook module that reads the sort order from the search-results store and wraps the setter so it also fires an analytics event. It is shared UI-state logic used by the sort dropdown and the column headers. It is a minor internal function; the store and the tracking module do the persistence and analytics work themselves.

A React context provider that wraps the app UI. It manages light/dark theme mode, applies the Ant Design ConfigProvider theme, and sets the body data-theme attribute. It is an app-wide UI theming component. Persistence is delegated to ThemeStorage helpers, so data_persistence is false.

A TypeScript props/type interface describing one item passed to the ActionsMenu component. It is a supporting type for a UI component's prop schema, not a component, view or action element in its own right, so it falls below modelling granularity. It holds data only and renders nothing.

PathElem is the in-memory domain model element for Jaeger's deep dependency graph (DDG). It holds path membership, operation, and visibility state, with only derived accessors and no I/O or business services. It is not persisted or published as a schema, so it is an application data object, notable within the DDG model module.

Trivial normalization helper that coerces a URL query param value into a string array; used only by resolveInitialFilter. Pure formatting utility with no architectural meaning on its own, below modelling granularity.

A small TypeScript interface carrying the parent/child/callCount dependency edge data, used locally by the DAGOptions UI component. It is a passive in-code data carrier and is not published as a schema, so it is an application data object of minor significance.

Bootstrap module that reads the <base> element to derive the site URL prefix and sets webpack's public path. This is configuration scaffolding: a small boot-time utility, not a named architectural element. It feeds routing indirectly but defines no routes, views or services.

Static method that merges two trace DAGs into a diff DAG with per-node A/B membership. It is core client-side computation behind the Trace Diff feature, so it is modelled as an internal application function. It does no telemetry emission, persistence or rendering itself.

A trivial type alias for the result of a URL query-string parsing utility. It is an implementation detail of a helper function, not a domain data structure or contract a maintainer would model as an architectural element.

A private static conversion helper that maps legacy tag key/value pairs to OTEL attribute objects inside the span facade constructor. It is a trivial data-mapping detail with no architectural identity. It handles trace data in the UI model, but it emits no telemetry itself.

Bootstraps client-side error capture for Jaeger UI: registers global error and unhandledrejection handlers and breadcrumb tracking, routing errors to a callback. This is telemetry instrumentation setup for application code paths, best modelled as an APM instrumentation configuration of moderate significance.

Immutable UI state holder recording which sections of the SpanDetail panel are expanded, with toggle methods returning new instances. It is a passive state carrier with trivial behaviour, not a view or a state machine. It is local to the SpanDetail component, so it is a minor data object.

A small enum of drag/mouse update type constants used internally by the DraggableManager UI utility. It is an implementation detail rather than a named architectural element. It holds no behaviour itself, so it implements none of the cross-cutting concerns.

This getter on a facade data-adapter class derives an instrumentation scope from legacy span tags. It is a small accessor and mapping detail with no callers. It displays trace data in a UI model rather than emitting telemetry, so it is not an architectural element and implements no cross-cutting concern itself.

A small internal TypeScript interface abstracting scrollTo/scrollBy for the ScrollManager in the trace page UI. It is an implementation-level abstraction with no callers, not something a maintainer would name as an architectural element. It does not render UI itself.

Small exported React sub-component of the common ErrorMessage widget that renders an error string as a heading. It is a reusable UI piece, but it is a minor part of the larger ErrorMessage component, so its architectural significance is low.

A hand-written HTTP client class: the Jaeger UI's single integration point to the query backend. It covers the v3 and legacy endpoints for services, operations, traces, metrics, dependencies and archive, with Zod response validation. It is a cohesive, replaceable component rather than one API contract, so it is modelled as an application component that integrates an external system.

DenseTrace is an in-memory derived representation of a trace for DAG building in Jaeger UI. Its constructor delegates the transform work to convSpans and makeDense, so the class itself mainly holds state consumed by TraceDag. That makes it an application data object, a notable internal unit of the trace-dag model rather than telemetry emission.

Plain TypeScript interface holding the search form's field values (service, operation, dates, tags, durations). It is a passive in-code data carrier for the SearchForm component and is not persisted or published as a schema. It matters only to its file and form logic, so it is a minor application data object.

This module is a test fixture holding one trace data case and its expected critical-path sections for the CriticalPath tests. It is test scaffolding that matters only to its own test file. It fits the testing layer, but no specific testing element type matches a single fixture data file well.

A formatting helper that converts microsecond durations to milliseconds and rounds them for one trace statistics table row. It is a pure value transformation, an implementation detail below architectural granularity, so it is not modelled as an element.

Private helper method of ScrollManager that computes a scroll offset and scrolls the trace view past a row. It is an internal UI scrolling implementation detail, below the granularity of an architecture element, though it does drive user-facing scroll behaviour.

Small utility module that walks parentSpan links to collect ancestor span IDs. It is a trivial helper in the Jaeger UI used for data traversal. It neither emits nor configures telemetry and is below architectural granularity.

A one-line analytics wrapper that forwards a fixed category/action pair to trackEvent. It is a trivial helper below modelling granularity. The observability work (sending usage analytics) is done by trackEvent, not by this symbol, so no concern is flagged.

Trivial accessor returning the wrapped legacy Trace object from the OtelTraceFacade. It is an escape-hatch getter with no logic, below the granularity of an architectural element. The facade class itself may be modelled, but this method is not.

A central in-memory domain type in Jaeger UI. It holds a transformed OTel trace: spans, a span map, root spans, services and derived display properties. It is passed between UI parts and is neither persisted nor published as a schema, so it is an application data object. It describes trace data rather than emitting telemetry, so observability is false.

A small utility module of memoized helpers for the TraceDiff graph. It computes a diff DAG of two traces and matches vertices against a search filter. This is internal application logic supporting a UI view, so it is classed as a minor application function rather than a UX element or telemetry.

A TypeScript props interface for the ActionsMenu React component. It is part of the component's prop schema and would be recorded as an attribute of the LibraryComponent, not as an element of its own. It is implementation boilerplate with no behaviour and no callers.

Internal helper class for the ListView virtualization component that tracks the heights and y-positions of rows. It is a layout calculation utility below architectural granularity and is used only by ListView and its test. It does no rendering itself.

A small analytics-tracking helper that emits a usage event (the parent/children toggle in the trace timeline) to the tracking backend. It is telemetry emission rather than application logic, but it is a minor per-interaction call site. Modelled at most as an APM event record of low significance.

Defines the client-side /monitor route path, its matcher, and URL query-parameter construction and parsing (service, spanKind, timeframe) for the Monitor view in the SPA router. This makes it a navigation route definition of moderate significance.

Trivial getter returning the length of an internal entries array on the Attributes model class. It is an accessor and implementation detail, not an architecturally meaningful element in its own right, and it does no telemetry, persistence or UI work.

An internal text-highlighting utility that builds regexes to split a string into highlighted segments for the FilteredList component. It is a helper below the granularity a maintainer would name in an architecture model, not a UI component itself.

An adapter that wraps Jaeger UI's legacy Trace in the IOtelTrace shape. Its constructor precomputes the span map, root spans, parent/child and link wiring, then exposes accessors. It is an in-memory domain data carrier for the trace viewer, not telemetry emission, so it is an application data object of moderate significance during the OTel migration.

A tiny local TypeScript interface with two string fields (content, title), used to carry form validation messages inside the SearchForm component. It has no callers and is an implementation detail of the UI form, not an architectural element in its own right.

Inline react-query queryFn callback within the useDeepDependencyGraphQuery hook. It only wires the client fetch, payload normalization and transformation together. This is an implementation detail of the hook rather than an element in its own right; the external call itself is made by JaegerClient.

Small scroll handler method on ScrollManager that scrolls the trace view up by roughly one page, used as a keyboard shortcut. It is a trivial UI helper below architectural granularity, though it does drive the user interface directly.

A small utility module wrapping the query-string library to normalize parsed URL query values (replacing nulls in arrays with empty strings). This is a trivial parsing helper with no architectural role, below the granularity of a model element.

A tiny result type carrying a single set of hidden span IDs, returned by the trace page's span filter. It is an internal data-carrying shape below the granularity a maintainer would name when explaining the architecture, with no callers listed, so it is not an element on its own.

Trivial one-line utility that returns the first key of a Map as the selected span ID for the timeline UI. It is a private-level helper with no architectural role, so it falls below element granularity.

Trivial getter on the OtelSpanFacade model class that returns whether the internal child span list is non-empty. It is an accessor and an implementation detail, so it is not an architectural element on its own.

A props type declaration for a UI list item component in a common FilteredList widget. It is a typing detail of a component's interface rather than a named architectural element. The component itself might be modelled as a UX librarycomponent, but its props interface is implementation detail.

React theme provider module wrapping antd ConfigProvider with light/dark theme configs and a theme-mode context. It is a reusable UI building block that drives app-wide presentation. Persistence of the chosen theme is delegated to ThemeStorage, so this module is UI-only. It is a notable but not core element.

An OpenTelemetry SpanProcessor registered in the tracer pipeline by initTracing. It stamps every span with page-path and session attributes following OTel's session conventions. The spec treats span processors as part of TraceConfiguration. It keeps session state in browser sessionStorage, which is a minor persistence concern.

A URL builder for the Monitor route: it merges query parameters onto ROUTE_PATH. It is navigation-related evidence for the Monitor route, but on its own it is only a small helper used by TopNav and the services view, so its significance is low.

Demo/mock data generator using Chance to fabricate random service dependency links. It is test/demo fixture scaffolding with no callers. It is minor, and no specific testing element type fits a random fake-data mixin.

Trivial getter returning a cached private field on the OtelSpanFacade model class. It is an accessor with no logic, below the granularity of an architectural element; the facade class itself would be the modelled element.

A small local TypeScript interface that groups the date and time string parameters used inside the search form. It has no callers and is a type-level implementation detail of the form, not an architecturally meaningful data object or schema.

Recursive helper that converts an OTel span tree into flamegraph nodes for the parent conversion function. It is a data-transformation implementation detail inside the flamegraph converter, not an architectural element. It only processes trace data for display and does not emit telemetry.

A computed getter on the PathElem model class that walks focal-side neighbours to build an ordered path list. It is an accessor-level implementation detail of a data structure, below the granularity an architecture model would record as its own element.

Memoized model transformation in Jaeger UI that converts fetched traces into deep dependency graph (DDG) path payloads for a focal service/operation. It is internal application behaviour (a data transformation function), notable within the DDG module but not a service boundary. It processes trace data but does not itself emit telemetry, so observability is false.

A trivial setter action in a Zustand UI-state store that writes the collapsed flag to localStorage and updates state. It is an implementation detail of the search panel store, below the granularity of a modelled element; it does touch durable browser storage.

A tiny TypeScript ref-handle interface exposing a single focusInput method for the FilteredList component. It is an implementation detail of a UI component's imperative API, not an architectural element on its own. It does not render anything itself.

Private HTTP transport helper in the JaegerClient API client: it wraps fetch with timeout and abort handling and converts failed responses into errors. It performs the external HTTP call itself but is an internal implementation detail of the client component, used by four public fetch methods, so it is a minor internal function.

A constants module holding layout limits, a fallback trace name and fetch-state string constants. These are implementation-detail values with no behaviour or contract of their own, so the module is not an architectural element.

A TypeScript interface in Jaeger UI's OTel domain types that holds a resource's attributes and service name. It is a passive in-code data structure that carries trace data for display. It is neither persisted nor published as a schema, and it emits no telemetry itself, so it is an application data object of modest significance.

A trivial getter that formats a debug/key string for a PathElem instance. It is pure formatting boilerplate with no callers and no behavior of architectural interest, so it falls below the model's granularity threshold.

A React component rendering a small group of expand/collapse icon buttons with tooltips inside the trace timeline header row. It is a non-routable UI fragment owned by one parent and used only there, so it is minor architecturally. It renders user-facing UI.

A tiny UI-state update type with a single cursor field, used in the TracePage view-range state. It is an implementation detail below the granularity of an architectural element. It has no callers, implements no behaviour and has no cross-cutting concerns.

Reusable UI utility class in Jaeger UI that manages mouse drag interactions (bounds, drag start/move/end callbacks) for timeline components. It is a notable internal unit rather than a view or component definition, so it is modelled as an application component that drives user interaction.

A one-line Zustand persist-middleware option selecting which state slice (explicitPrefs) is saved. It is store configuration boilerplate, not an architectural element. It only defines the slice, while the persist middleware performs the actual storage, so data_persistence is not attributed.

A trivial immutable state toggle on the DetailState UI state class. It copies the state and flips the events-section open flag. This is an implementation detail below architectural granularity and does not render UI itself.

A tiny module exporting one string-formatting helper that builds an aria-label for comparison checkboxes. It is a trivial formatting utility below the granularity of an architecture element and renders nothing itself.

A passive in-memory data structure carrying precomputed per-value span counts and range values for the span filter popover. It is neither persisted nor published as a schema, so it is an application data object. It is minor and local to the span filter module.

A trivial setter on ScrollManager that only assigns the accessors field. It is an implementation detail: it has no behaviour of its own and is not an architectural element a maintainer would name when explaining the system.

A tiny analytics helper that fires a UI-tracking event when the span detail tags panel is toggled. It is one of many similar per-event trackers. It counts as observability (usage tracking) work, but sits below the granularity of a modelled element. The broader tracking module would be the element, not this function.

A React hook module that manages the client-side singleton cache of file-uploaded traces in the Jaeger UI search page. It is a notable internal state-management unit. It renders nothing itself, and it uses only in-memory React Query storage, so it does not perform durable persistence.

A tiny internal TypeScript interface holding name, message and stack for error tracking. It is a trivial helper data shape used only within the error-capture utility, below the granularity a maintainer would name as an architectural element. It does no telemetry work itself.

A React UI component that renders a popover hops selector, with increment and decrement buttons, in the Deep Dependencies header. It is a reusable component definition taking props, so it belongs to the ux layer. It is a minor sub-part of the header. Its call to trackHopChange is analytics tracking delegated to another symbol, so observability is false.

A trivial property setter on the OtelSpanFacade data wrapper that only assigns a private field. It is an accessor and an implementation detail, below the granularity of an architectural element. It handles span data in the UI model but does not itself emit or configure telemetry.

A tiny React render function used as the AssistantMessage slot of a thread component map. It wraps the shared message body in an assistant-styled row. It is a UI component, but it is minor and only its file cares about it, so it rates significance 1.

A small UI state type in the Jaeger TracePage that describes the zoom and drag range of the timeline view. It is local component state plumbing that only carries data, sits below model granularity and is not a data-model entity, so it is not modelled as an element.

Small GraphModel method that maps vertex keys to path elements and delegates to getVisWithElems to compute a visibility encoding. It is an internal helper of the deep dependency graph model, below the granularity a maintainer would name as an architectural element.

Module of UX analytics tracking functions for the Deep Dependencies view. It defines event categories and actions and emits usage-tracking events through trackEvent. This makes it a manual instrumentation site for user-interaction telemetry, though only a minor unit local to one component.

A small local TypeScript type that describes one error variant of the fetch state in the DeepDependencies view. It is an implementation detail of the component's state typing. It has no callers and no independent architectural identity, so it should not be modelled as an element.

A demo/test data generator that uses Chance to fabricate random Jaeger traces for demos and tests. It is test-data scaffolding rather than production telemetry. It is not a coverage-model artifact, so no testing element type fits. It is minor and has no callers.

Trivial accessor returning a node from an in-memory map on TraceDag; it has no behaviour of its own beyond a lookup. It is an implementation detail below the granularity of an architecture element, so it is not modelled as an element.

A trivial lookup helper that maps a long time-unit name to its short abbreviation for display formatting. It is a formatting utility below the granularity of an architectural element, so it is not modelled.

A formatting helper that shapes error data into Google Analytics event fields (truncation, string assembly). It belongs to the error-tracking pipeline, so it supports observability, but it is a pure formatter below modelling granularity. The trackErrorData caller or the GA tracking module would be the apm element.

This client-side module computes a trace-wide GenAI execution summary by aggregating span classifications and token usage. Jaeger UI uses it to analyse trace data, but it does not emit telemetry itself, so it is internal application behaviour rather than an apm element. A maintainer would name it when explaining the trace header.

A public method on the DDG GraphModel that toggles the visibility of a vertex's generation (upstream or downstream neighbours) by recomputing the visibility encoding. It is internal model logic, a minor behavioural unit within the GraphModel component, and does no persistence, I/O or rendering of its own.

React module rendering the service dependency DAG via the plexus Digraph. It includes node rendering and a context menu for setting focus and viewing traces. It is a reusable, non-routable visualization component embedded in the DependencyGraph page, so it is best modelled as a UX library component of moderate significance.

Small internal helper that reads the embedded Jaeger UI config from a window global, falling back to the defaults. It is called only by getConfig, which is the meaningful configuration entry point. On its own it is an implementation detail; the console.warn does not amount to an observability concern.

Exported TypeScript contract for pluggable web-analytics providers in Jaeger UI, covering init, enablement, page-view, error and event tracking. It is the integration seam behind which tracking implementations such as Google Analytics sit, so it is best modelled as an application interface. Its purpose is usage telemetry, so observability applies.

A one-line wrapper on the JaegerClient API client that delegates to fetchJson with a fixed error message. It is a trivial method below modelling granularity. Any external-integration modelling belongs to the JaegerClient component or to fetchJson, not to this method, which does no HTTP work itself.

Module whose main export transforms Jaeger trace HTTP response data into the app's internal Trace model. It deduplicates span IDs, links parents and children, and repairs start times. This is a notable internal data-transformation function in the UI's model layer. It processes telemetry data but does not itself emit telemetry.

A tiny internal state type (done/value) for the Tween animation helper in the trace page UI. It is an implementation detail of a scrolling-animation utility, not an architecturally meaningful element in any layer.

Central in-memory domain type of the Jaeger UI's OTEL trace model. It carries span state plus derived tree properties (depth, childSpans, relativeStartTime) and has no behaviour or published schema, so it is an application DataObject. It is not APM telemetry, because the UI only displays spans and does not emit them.

React component rendering one GenAI message (collapsible header, per-part format controls, bodies) inside the GenAI tab of span detail. It is a non-routable fragment within a parent view, so it is a UX subview. It is a minor internal unit of that tab with no external callers and only UI concerns.

Main webpack entrypoint of the Jaeger UI SPA. It bootstraps the React root, mounts the BrowserRouter and App, and initializes tracing and tracking. It is the front-end application root, so it is a core entry point modelled as the UX application. It calls tracing setup but does not itself implement observability.

A trivial React props interface declaring only a children prop for a query-client provider wrapper. It is boilerplate typing below the granularity of an architecture element and carries no behaviour or cross-cutting concern.

Generated/handwritten API client method bound to GET /api/v3/traces/{trace_id}; per the spec, a client method bound to a distinct method+path is an api Operation. It calls the Jaeger query backend over HTTP and validates the response envelope, and it is a key integration point used by several UI callers.

A trivial formatting helper that builds a page title string from the operation and service names of the trace's root span. It is a display-string utility called during trace data transformation, an implementation detail rather than an architectural element.

React lifecycle cleanup method that disposes the component's draggable managers. It is a trivial implementation detail of the ViewingLayer UI component and not an architectural element in its own right.

A 911-line module that parses OTel GenAI span attributes (messages, tool calls, token usage, retrieval, memory, agent data) into typed view models for the GenAI tab. It is a cohesive data-extraction and transformation function within the Jaeger UI. It does not emit telemetry itself, and it does not render anything.

A small data shape carrying error-tracking context (breadcrumbs, tags, URL) that is attached to captured errors in Jaeger UI's tracking utilities. It belongs to the telemetry concern, but it is only a payload type, not an instrument or configuration. No APM element type fits it, and it has low significance.
A one-line math helper that maps a slider position to a value on a logarithmic scale inside a UI range facet. It is a private implementation detail with no architectural meaning on its own.

An API client method bound to one HTTP endpoint (GET deep-dependencies) on the Jaeger backend. The layer guidance treats generated or handwritten API client methods tied to a distinct method and path as Operation evidence. It is a thin wrapper that issues an external HTTP call, so its significance is moderate.

Utility module implementing Jaeger UI's text-based span search/filter logic (include/exclude terms over span names, services, tags, logs). It is internal application behaviour supporting the trace search feature, not telemetry emission itself. It is a notable unit a maintainer would name, but not a service boundary.

An inline arrow function that composes link-formatting functions via reduce. It is a trivial formatting utility and an implementation detail inside link-formatting.ts. It has no callers and is not an architectural element. The callee edge to a test fn is a spurious resolution artifact.

A trivial React props interface with a single trace field for the TraceFlamegraph component. It is an implementation detail of the component's contract, not an architectural element on its own. Any modelling would happen on the component itself, as a ux component, not on its props type.

A small private drag-event handler inside the ViewingLayer UI component. It computes a reframe anchor and shift and forwards them through a prop callback. It drives UI interaction state, but as an implementation detail it is below the granularity of an architecture element.

TypeScript interface describing the shape of a React context value for the Jaeger assistant panel (open state, bootstrap text, callbacks). It is a passive in-code data-carrying type, not a published schema, so it is an application data object of minor significance.

A React module defining a small reusable sparkline area-chart component (OperationsGraph). It is used inside the operations details table of the Monitor services view. It takes color, data points, y-domain and error props and renders a chart or a placeholder. It is a minor UI building block, not a screen.

A one-line wrapper that forwards a fixed analytics category and action to trackEvent. It is a trivial helper below the granularity of an architectural element. The analytics call happens in trackEvent, so this symbol does not itself implement observability.

Private animation-frame callback inside a Tween utility class used for scroll animation in the trace page. It is an implementation detail of the tweening helper, not something a maintainer would name as an architectural element.

Module of heuristic transforms that normalize dense span nodes (fixing service and operation names, marking skippable spans) when building the trace DAG in Jaeger UI. It is internal application logic that processes trace data rather than emitting telemetry. It is a minor internal unit of the trace-dag model with no callers recorded.

A small internal type pairing a verb and a criterion for the trace page's span-filter logic. It is a local data-shape detail with no callers and no published schema, so it sits below the granularity of an architecture element.

A tiny higher-order helper that builds a string hash of a path element's focal path for deduplicating nodes in the dependency-graph model. It is an internal implementation detail below the level a maintainer would name as an architectural element.

A trivial getter on OtelTraceFacade that returns the wrapped legacy trace's endTime with a type cast. It is an accessor and implementation detail, not an architectural element. It handles trace data, but it does not itself emit telemetry or implement any other cross-cutting concern.

Module of string constants naming OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic-convention span attribute keys used by the Jaeger UI to interpret traces. It holds only constants, emits no telemetry and has no behaviour of its own, so it is an implementation detail rather than an architectural element.

A small exported TypeScript interface in the Jaeger UI's OTel type definitions that describes the key/value shape of a telemetry attribute. As a domain data shape it fits data-model objectschema, but it is a minor structural type with no behaviour, so significance is low.

Trivial alias method on a UI detail-state class that simply delegates to toggleEventItem. It has no callers and no logic of its own, which makes it a backward-compatibility wrapper below modelling granularity.
A module exporting a single string constant used as a test/DOM marker for the search results component. It is a trivial constant, not an architecturally meaningful element in any layer.

A small options interface for initialising the error-capture utility. It holds an onError callback and a tags map. It is a supporting type for the tracking module and has no callers or behaviour, so it sits below the granularity of an architecture element. Being only a type, it performs no telemetry work itself.

Small React presentational component that renders the tooltip body (a heading plus a truncated span list) for the span bar row. It is a UI element, but a minor one used only within its file, so its architectural significance is low. It displays trace data rather than producing telemetry.

A one-line local callback inside the TraceDiffHeader React component. It toggles the visibility of the B-side cohort table popover by delegating to toggleTable. It is a trivial UI state helper below the granularity of an architectural element; the containing component would be the modelled UX element.

Private lazy-index helper that builds an in-memory first-wins lookup map for the Attributes class; called only by its sibling accessors. It is an implementation detail below architectural granularity, with no cross-cutting concern. It handles telemetry attribute data in memory but emits no telemetry itself.

One-line wrapper that forwards a fixed category/action pair to the shared trackEvent analytics utility. It is a trivial helper below the granularity of an architecture model. The real telemetry work happens in trackEvent, so this symbol does not itself implement observability.

A TypeScript function-type interface describing the factory signature for creating a web analytics tracker. It is a type-level contract detail with no behaviour, no callers, and sits below the granularity a maintainer would name. The analytics implementation itself would carry any observability concern, not this signature type.

A small utility module in Jaeger UI that serializes traces to JSON and triggers a browser file download. It is an internal helper behind a 'download traces' capability rather than a UI view or a telemetry element. It writes a downloadable file and drives a browser interaction, so it is minor application functionality.

onStart is the SpanProcessor hook of PageAttributionProcessor. It enriches each span with the page path and session attributes, and persists session state to browser storage. It is a method inside an APM span processor, not a standalone element. The containing processor would be modelled instead, so no element type is assigned and significance is low.

A TypeScript interface that holds aggregated GenAI call counts computed from trace spans and is consumed by the trace page header. It is a passive in-code data carrier, not persisted and not published as a schema, so it is an application data object of minor significance.

Config loader module that merges compile-time defaults, the embedded UI config injected by query-service, and backend capabilities, then memoizes the result. It is a notable internal application function a maintainer would name when explaining UI configuration. It does no persistence or external calls itself: it only reads window globals.

A single action in a Zustand UI state store for the trace timeline. It collapses every span that has children by updating the childrenHiddenIDs set. This is a minor implementation detail of view state, below the granularity of an architectural element. It drives UI display state only.

Internal mouse-event dispatch method of the DraggableManager UI utility; translates DOM drag events into update callbacks. An implementation detail of a UI helper class, not an architectural element on its own, though it directly drives user-interface interaction.

A tiny TypeScript interface with a single numeric field. It carries a time-shift update payload inside the TracePage UI state. It is an implementation detail with no callers, below the granularity of an architectural element, so it is not modelled.

Utility module that detects, normalizes and validates uploaded OTLP trace JSON files against v3 schemas before loading into the UI. It is internal parsing/normalization behaviour, an application function a maintainer would name when explaining trace upload. It is not telemetry emission itself, and it performs no storage or external calls.

A trivial string helper that prepends the site path prefix to a URL. It is widely called, but it is a formatting utility with no architectural identity, so it falls below the granularity of a modelled element.

A trivial two-field local type holding start/end timestamp strings for the search form. It is an internal helper return-type shape with no callers, below the granularity a maintainer would name in an architecture model.

Private helper of ColorGenerator that assigns and caches a round-robin color index per key in an in-memory map. It is a trivial implementation detail for UI coloring, not an architectural element, and it touches no durable storage or external systems.

A small internal closure inside the ClickToCopy component. It copies text to the clipboard and updates local state flags. This is a private UI implementation detail, not an architectural element. The enclosing component would be the modelled UX element, not this handler.

The module defines the SpanGraph React component. It is the trace minimap shown in the TracePage header, composing TickLabels, CanvasSpanGraph and ViewingLayer. It is a non-routable UI region of the trace view, so it fits a subview. It is a notable UI unit, but it does not emit telemetry; it only renders trace data.

Private rendering helper inside the ViewingLayer React component that returns SVG rect markers for the drag highlight. It is an implementation detail of the component's render method and not an architectural element on its own, though it does render UI.

A small local TypeScript interface holding tooltip position and display values for the flamegraph component's internal UI state. It is an implementation detail with no callers or architectural role, below the granularity of a modelled element.

This is a small utility module with two pure helpers that deduplicate and sort span attribute key-value pairs for display in the Jaeger UI. It holds no architectural contract, service or schema, so it is an implementation detail rather than a modelled element. It does not emit telemetry itself; it only processes trace data.

Small analytics-tracking helper that maps a graph direction to a UI analytics event via trackEvent. It is a thin wrapper below the granularity of an architecture element; the tracking utility, not this function, would be modelled. It emits usage telemetry, so it touches observability.

An immutable state-toggle helper on the DetailState UI state holder. It only adds or removes an event item from a set of expanded items. This is an implementation detail of the span detail panel's expand/collapse state, not an architectural element in its own right.

Small UI utility module binding keyboard shortcuts via a Combokeys singleton for the TracePage. It drives user input (keyboard triggers mapped to handlers), loosely a reusable interaction pattern, but it is a minor internal helper only the TracePage cares about.

A trivial one-line normalization helper that maps a legacy 'all operations' sentinel to the current constant for the search form. It is an implementation detail with no architectural identity of its own, so it is not modelled as an element.

Trivial static factory method that just constructs a MatchHighlighter instance. It is boilerplate below the architectural granularity threshold, has no callers, and implements no cross-cutting concern itself.

A small TypeScript interface describing the shape of an OTel span event (timestamp, name, attributes) inside the Jaeger UI. It is an in-code data carrier with no behaviour. It is not persisted or published as a schema, and it does not emit telemetry itself. Minor internal data type.

Module that transforms an OTel trace into a hierarchical flame-graph data structure, aggregating spans by name and adjusting layout values. It is internal data-transformation behaviour supporting the flamegraph view. It is not itself rendering or emitting telemetry, so it is an application function of notable but module-level significance.

A tiny two-field type describing a config key rename, used only by the config deprecation helper. It is an implementation detail of config processing, below the granularity a maintainer would name as an architectural element.

A client-side state-store action (Zustand-style) that removes view modifiers from in-memory DDG state keyed by entry. It is internal behaviour of the DeepDependencies store and minor in scope. It manipulates only transient UI state, not durable storage, and renders nothing itself.

Private UI event handler inside the ViewingLayer component that finalizes a scrubber drag and updates the view range. It is an implementation detail of a UX component, not an architectural element on its own, though it drives the user interface.

A props type declaration for the internal SearchForm implementation component. It is a typing detail of a UI component rather than a standalone architectural element, so it would be captured as attributes of the ux component, not as a node of its own.

Barrel module that re-exports the track middleware and wraps redux-promise-middleware under a new name. It contains no logic of its own and is wiring boilerplate rather than an architectural element. The tracking concern lives in track.ts, not here.

Internal helper method of the virtualized list Positions class that computes cached row heights and y-offsets. It is a layout-calculation implementation detail, below the granularity of an architectural element, with no cross-cutting concerns of its own.

A one-line accessor that delegates to setClauseValues to extract the hidden service names from a span filter. It is a trivial helper wrapper sitting below the granularity of an architectural element, even though several UI hooks and tests call it.

A plain in-code data structure carrying aggregated flamegraph table row values (service, name, count, self/total time) for a UI table. It is neither persisted nor published as a schema, so it is an application data object of minor, file-local significance.

The module defines the client-side '/search' route path (ROUTE_PATH), its matcher, and URL builders and parsers for the search page's query-string state. That makes it the SPA route definition for the Search Trace page, a notable navigation element. It does not render UI or persist data, so no cross-cutting concern applies.

Trivial one-line helper that falls back from trace name to trace ID for sorting search results. It is an implementation detail used only by sort comparators in the same file, so it is not an architectural element.

A small internal helper in the virtualized list's Positions class. It incrementally computes row heights and y-offsets up to a given y value. This is an implementation detail of the UI layout math, not an architectural element, and it renders nothing itself.

Small pure helper that normalizes the TraceDiff state. It deduplicates the cohort trace IDs and fills in defaults for selections a and b. This is an implementation detail of the TraceDiff UI module, below the level a maintainer would name as an architectural element.

A small TypeScript interface in Jaeger UI's OTel type definitions that holds a span's status code and message. It is a passive data structure carried through the UI code, so it is best modelled as an application data object. It has minor significance and does no telemetry work itself.

Internal helper method of the ListView Positions class. It recalculates cached row heights and y-offsets for virtualized list rendering. This is an implementation detail of layout computation, not an architectural element. It renders nothing itself, so it carries no UI concern.

A local closure inside a panel resize handler. It resets the cursor and user-select styles and removes the drag event listeners. This is a trivial UI implementation detail below architectural granularity. It touches the user interface only by restoring document styles.

A tiny local TypeScript interface holding two optional start/end strings for the search form's query parameters. It has no callers, carries no behaviour, and is an implementation detail of the form component rather than a nameable architectural element.

A factory returning SVG and HTML node-decoration render callbacks (borders, find-match emphasis) for the Deep Dependencies graph. It is UI rendering code, but it sits below the granularity of a view or library component. It is a minor internal helper used by the graph component, so no element type fits.
A trivial getter on the PathElem class that returns a private field and throws if it is unset. It is an accessor and an implementation detail, below the granularity of an architecture element.

React hook that programmatically redirects the trace page URL to the canonical trace ID using replace navigation. It is a client-side route change (a programmatic redirect within one route), so it fits navigation. It is a minor unit, significant only to the TracePage module.

A TypeScript interface that only carries aggregated span-statistics row data for the Trace Statistics table in Jaeger UI. It has no behaviour, is not persisted, and is not published as a schema, so it is an application DataObject of minor, file-local significance.

Trivial formatting helper that converts an unknown value into a displayable attribute string for GenAI tab tool-call rendering. It is an implementation detail below architectural granularity and does no rendering, persistence or telemetry work itself.

A barrel module that re-exports the Zustand stores for the trace timeline viewer and adds one coordinating function for detail panel mode. It is the client-side state management unit for the timeline UI, so it is modelled as an application component of moderate significance. It holds UI state rather than persisting it.

Trivial toString override that serializes the PathElem via toJSON for string interpolation. It is a formatting helper with no architectural meaning on its own and sits below the granularity of any modelled element.

A small TypeScript interface describing the shape of an error-tracking breadcrumb (Sentry-style) inside a tracking utility. It is a plain internal data shape with no callers listed and no behaviour, so it sits below architectural granularity. It supports telemetry but does not itself emit any.

A small React hooks module that derives AI-assistant feature-flag state from backend-advertised config and the AG-UI endpoint URL. It is internal feature-gating logic rather than a UI view or an API contract. It is minor, so it is modelled as an application function of low significance.

An inner event handler inside the DependencyGraph React component. It normalizes the depth input value and updates local state, with debouncing. This is an implementation detail of a UI view, not an architectural element in its own right. It drives UI state only.

Trivial accessor on the Attributes model class that returns the keys of an internal index. It is an implementation detail with no callers and no architectural role of its own, so it would not be recorded as an element.

A small TypeScript interface describing the 'done' variant of a fetch-state union local to the DeepDependencies component. It is a typing detail inside the component file, below the granularity a maintainer would name as an architectural element.

A constants module defining keyboard key string literals that replace a third-party enum. It is a trivial implementation detail with no behaviour, no callers recorded and no architectural role, so it is not modelled as an element.

React presentational component that renders timeline tick marks and duration labels in the trace timeline header. It is a reusable UI building block with its own props, used by TimelineHeaderRow. It is a minor visual detail within the TracePage view, so its significance is low.

Ambient TypeScript type declaration for a third-party d3 flame graph library (external-modules.d.ts). It has no callers and only provides typings for an external dependency, so it is typing scaffolding rather than an architectural element in its own right.

A small analytics-tracking module that defines event categories and thin wrappers emitting UI usage events through trackEvent for the trace page header. It is telemetry, so the closest fit is apm event records. Because it is file-local and has minor scope, significance is low.

A trivial accessor on the Attributes collection class that delegates a key-existence check to an internal index map. It is an implementation detail below modelling granularity, so it is not an architectural element and implements none of the cross-cutting concerns.

SpanPill is a small reusable React UI component that renders a span attribute pill with a tooltip in the trace timeline. It is a UX building block with a props contract, but it is minor and only relevant within the span bar row rendering. It renders UI; it does not emit telemetry itself.

A private helper that converts a mouse clientX into a clamped relative position for the drag manager. It is pure arithmetic and an implementation detail below the level an architecture model would record.
A tiny module exporting a single string constant used as a test/DOM marker for the search form submit button. It is a trivial constant with no architectural meaning on its own.

Tiny React render component supplied as the UserMessage slot of the assistant thread. It only wraps the message body in a styled row. It is a UI building block, but too trivial to be architecturally significant beyond its file.

An ambient type declaration in an external-modules .d.ts file, typing a third-party flame graph library's node shape. It is a typing shim for a dependency with no callers, not an architectural element. The data structure is trivial and generated-like, so it sits below modelling granularity.

Small internal method of the virtualized-list Positions helper that resizes its cached y-value and height arrays to match the data length. It is an implementation detail of list rendering, not an architectural element, and implements no cross-cutting concern itself.

Barrel module that only re-exports the GenAI span detection utility from './detect' to preserve an import path. It contains no behaviour of its own and is boilerplate, so it is not an architectural element.

Trivial TypeScript wrapper interface holding only the UI view-range time state for the trace page. It is an internal UI state type with no callers or behaviour, so it falls below the granularity an architecture model records.

Inline cell-render closure inside the TraceStatistics table component that formats a cell or wraps the name cell in a clickable span. This is a trivial presentational helper below modelling granularity. It does render UI, but it is not an architectural element.
Trivial accessor on DraggableManager that returns a private flag. It has no callers and no logic, so it is an implementation detail and not an architectural element.

Module declaring two branded numeric type aliases (Microseconds, Milliseconds) for compile-time type safety. These are implementation-level typing utilities, not domain entities or schemas a maintainer would name as architectural elements, and they have no callers or callees.

Trivial local UI state shape (x, y, name) for a flamegraph context menu. It is an implementation detail of the component, with no callers or architectural role, so it falls below the model's granularity threshold.

A Zustand persist-middleware merge callback that combines rehydrated layout preferences with the current store state. It is a small configuration helper inside the layout store, an implementation detail below the granularity of an architecture element. It only reshapes in-memory state; storage I/O is handled by the middleware, not by this function.

Private helper method within GraphModel that computes adjacent-generation path elements for a vertex. It is internal graph traversal logic used only by sibling methods, so it falls below the granularity of an architectural element.

Utility module in Jaeger UI's critical path computation. It converts OTel spans into CPSpan structures and prunes non-blocking branches. This is internal application logic supporting the critical-path algorithm, not telemetry emission itself. It is a minor internal unit, so it is modelled as an application function.

A small TypeScript interface holding the state of a span filter (clauses and tree mode) in the Jaeger UI trace page. It is a passive in-code data structure with no behaviour, so it is an application data object. It is of minor significance, local to the span filtering module.

A test-only helper that resets the module-level variables of the error-capture tracking module. It is scaffolding for testing, called only from the test file, and below the granularity of an architectural element. It performs no telemetry itself.

A trivial accessor on a UI color-assignment utility that maps a key to a palette color. Many UI components call it, but it is a presentational helper below architectural granularity. It does no rendering of its own, so no concerns apply.

A small readonly interface describing a time-range dropdown option (label, lookback string, milliseconds) in a utils file, with no callers. It is a trivial configuration-shaped type below the granularity a maintainer would name. It is neither a published schema nor a meaningful data object.

Utility module encoding and decoding deep-dependency-graph vertex visibility into compact base36 strings, used for URL state. It is internal application logic within the DDG model with no persistence, UI or integration of its own. It is a minor unit that a maintainer might name only when explaining the DDG module.

Trivial immutable state-toggle method on a UI detail-state value class: it clones the state and flips a boolean flag. It is an implementation detail below architectural granularity, with no callers in the graph and no cross-cutting work of its own.

React component rendering the trace DAG graph view (Digraph with layers, mode buttons, help) within the TracePage; it is a non-routable region of the trace page view, so modelled as a UX subview. It visualizes trace data but does not emit telemetry itself.

React module defining the span/service filter popover component (SpanFilterButton) in the trace timeline viewer; a reusable UI component with props, composing FacetList, RangeFacet and Section. It is a notable UI element within the TracePage, not a routable view.

A trivial React context accessor hook that wraps the optional variant and throws when no provider is present. It is boilerplate below the granularity of an architecture element. The context or provider would be modelled instead, not this accessor.

Barrel index file that only re-exports the default TraceDiffGraph component. It is module boilerplate with no behaviour of its own, so it is not an architectural element; the TraceDiffGraph component itself would be modelled in the ux layer instead.

A reusable React component in components/common that renders trace-level external links, either as a single link or as a dropdown menu. It is a UI building block with a props contract, not a routable view, and is used by TracePageHeader. Significance is moderate.

A computed getter on the PathElem DDG model class that walks the external-side neighbor chain and returns the path, reversed for negative distance. It is an accessor and traversal helper inside a data structure, below the granularity of an architectural element.

Private helper inside the DDG GraphModel that decodes a visibility encoding into path elements, falling back to defaults. It is an implementation detail of the graph model's internal logic, below the granularity a maintainer would name as an architectural element.
Trivial accessor that checks whether a node ID exists in the TraceDag's in-memory map. It is used only by addNode, so it is an implementation detail and not an architectural element.

Small presentational helper component inside the GenAITab that renders a JSON value as a tree or a pre block. It is a private rendering detail of the tab view rather than a reusable library component or a view, so it is not modelled as an element.

A static configuration table that maps keyboard shortcuts to trace-page UI actions. It is a UI interaction convention: keyboard input triggers scroll, pan, zoom and collapse. It is constant data with no logic, so it would at most be recorded as a minor ux action pattern. It supports the user interface but does little work itself.

Small UI module that defines a SpanPill presentational component (an antd Tag inside a Tooltip) and a config hook that enables the feature. It is a reusable UI building block of the trace timeline row, but a minor one that only nearby files care about. It renders UI and does not emit telemetry itself.

Cleanup/teardown method on a UI drag helper utility: removes a window listener and nulls callbacks. This is lifecycle boilerplate below the granularity of an architectural element, so it is not modelled on its own.

Trivial DOM helper returning the scroll offset of a window or element, used only by sibling scroll functions in the same file. It is an implementation detail with no architectural meaning on its own and does not itself render UI.

Module defining a reusable collapsible Section UI component, plus a KeepControl tooltip wrapper, used inside the span filter popover. It is a small presentational building block with props and children slots. It is a UX library component of minor significance, local to the ServiceFilter feature.

Pure formatting helper that picks the largest time unit fitting a microsecond duration for display. It is a trivial utility with no architectural role, persistence, integration or telemetry emission of its own, so it is not an architecture-model element.

A small text-formatting helper method that applies regex matchers to highlight search matches in a filtered list item. It is a UI rendering utility below architectural granularity, used only by ListItem and its test, so it is not a model element.

Test fixture module providing a transformed trace and expected critical path sections for critical-path computation tests. It belongs to the testing layer as fixture data, but no listed testing element type fits a single fixture case precisely. It has minor significance, mattering only to its test suite.

DetailsCard is a reusable React UI component in components/common. It declares a props schema (header, description, details, collapsible) and renders either a list or a table. That makes it a library component definition rather than a placed instance. It is a modest shared building block with limited architectural weight.

No-op forceFlush stub that satisfies the OpenTelemetry SpanProcessor interface by returning a resolved promise. It does no telemetry work itself and is boilerplate below modelling granularity. The parent processor class would be the apm element.

Module defining analytics tracking event categories/actions for TracePage UI interactions (filter, match navigation, range changes), emitting via trackEvent. It is user-analytics telemetry instrumentation for one page; minor, file-local significance. Best fit is apm instrumentation of a code path.

A one-line normalization helper that reshapes OTLP attribute arrays during trace file upload parsing. It is a private data-transformation detail below the granularity of an architectural element, with no callers recorded.

Trivial getter on a facade class that delegates to the wrapped legacy trace's services property. It is an accessor and implementation detail with no behaviour of its own, so it falls below the modelling granularity threshold.

A utility module of pure helper functions for the trace timeline viewer's UI state: collapse checks, find-row focus states and detail subsection toggles. It is an implementation detail supporting UI components, not a nameable architectural element on its own.

A tiny inline keyboard event handler inside a context menu component that closes the menu on Escape. It is an implementation detail of the UI component, not an architectural element on its own, though it does drive user interface behaviour.

A small helper method on a Tween animation utility. It computes the current eased value from elapsed time. This is an implementation detail of scroll animation in the trace page, not an architecturally meaningful element on its own.

React hook module that resolves the configured path-agnostic decoration schema, fetches decoration summaries from external URLs via the API client using react-query caching, tracks session maxima and returns presentation data. It is a notable internal data-fetching/behaviour unit rather than a UI view or API contract. It integrates with external decoration endpoints; the cache is in-memory, not durable.

A one-line analytics wrapper that sends a UI toggle event for the process section through the shared trackEvent utility. It is a trivial helper below modelling granularity. The tracking work itself happens in trackEvent, so this function implements no cross-cutting concern on its own.

A small module of local TypeScript type aliases (TSumSpan, TEv) that describe the graph data consumed by the TraceGraph UI component. It is internal typing scaffolding, not a published schema or architectural element in its own right, and has no callers or callees.

A no-op shutdown method that only resolves a promise. It is boilerplate required by the OpenTelemetry SpanProcessor interface on PageAttributionProcessor and has no behaviour of its own. The parent processor may be an apm element, but this method is an implementation detail.

Trivial accessor returning the private _entries array of the Attributes model class. It has no behaviour beyond exposing internal state, so it is an implementation detail rather than an architectural element.

A rendering helper that maps each metric quantile to a Recharts Area series with its own colour and stroke, so it is effectively a chart series configuration inside the service graph component. It is a minor internal unit used only by ServiceGraphImpl, and its only cross-cutting concern is rendering UI.

A small React component that renders the GenAI memory section (store, query, record count and records) inside the span detail GenAI tab. It is a non-routable UI fragment of a larger view and is a minor unit within the tab file. It renders a user interface but does not emit telemetry or persist data.

Module transforms validated OTLP wire data from the Jaeger v3 API into the enriched IOtelTrace UI model: time conversion, span kind/status mapping, attribute decoding and tree building. This is internal data-transformation behaviour, an application function behind the API client. It processes trace data but emits no telemetry itself, so observability is false.

Empty no-op implementation of the SpanProcessor onEnd interface method. It is required boilerplate for the processor contract and does no work. The parent PageAttributionProcessor may be an APM element, but this method itself is not architecturally meaningful and implements no concern.

Module computing trace statistics table values (per-service/operation/attribute aggregates of span durations and self-time) for the TracePage statistics view. It is client-side analysis logic feeding a UI table rather than a UI component or telemetry emitter, so it is best modelled as an internal application function of moderate significance.

Small React component rendering the Jaeger logo and name as a link to the home route. It is a UI building block (likely placed in the top nav). It has minor architectural significance and only implements a user interface concern.

A generic animation tweening utility using requestAnimationFrame and an easing function, used for scroll animation in the trace page. It is a low-level UI helper rather than a view, component, or transition template a maintainer would name architecturally, so it is not modelled as an element.

Private helper that writes a key/value to sessionStorage while swallowing privacy-mode errors. It is an implementation detail of the PageAttributionProcessor span processor, not an architectural element on its own. It does write to browser session storage, so data_persistence applies.

A color-lookup helper method on a ColorGenerator utility. It resolves a key to RGB values, reading CSS variables where present. This is a presentation implementation detail rather than an architectural element, so it would not be recorded as a node in the model.

This is a URL-state codec helper: it decodes a checksum and bitmask query value into the set of visible services for the trace timeline. It is internal application logic with some navigation flavour. It is a minor unit, modelled at most as an application function, and implements no cross-cutting concern itself.

A small React link component in the Jaeger trace page. It renders an anchor that either focuses a span in the same trace or opens another trace URL in a new tab. It is a user-operable navigation trigger, so it is a UX action component of minor significance.

A trivial Redux action-creator payload mapper in the TraceTimelineViewer duck, returning { spans } for the COLLAPSE_ALL action type. It is boilerplate below architectural granularity and has no callers, callees or cross-cutting behaviour of its own.

An internal in-memory graph mutation method on the TraceDag data structure. It adds a node and links it to its parent. This is an implementation detail of the DAG model, not an architectural element on its own, and it does no persistence or I/O.

A string-formatting helper that builds a truncated, comma-separated summary of tool labels for the GenAI tab's ToolsSection. It is a trivial formatting utility below architectural granularity. It feeds UI text but renders nothing itself, so no concern applies.
Trivial reset method on a color generator utility that clears an in-memory cache and index; only called from tests. An implementation detail with no architectural meaning on its own.

Type module defining the web analytics tracking contract (page views, errors, events) and its factory. It is the abstraction behind the UI's usage telemetry plug-in, so it fits as instrumentation configuration in APM. It contains only type definitions, which gives it moderate significance.

Barrel index module that only re-exports the TraceDiff component's default export. It is boilerplate with no behaviour of its own; the TraceDiff view itself would be the modelled UX element, not this re-export file.

Utility module of sorting comparators and mappings between table column sort state and OrderBy values for search results. It is a helper-level implementation detail supporting the search results UI, not an architectural element on its own.

A small cleanup method on an animation tweening helper. It clears timers and animation frames and resets its callbacks. This is an implementation detail of a scroll-animation utility, not an architecturally meaningful element. It only supports UI animation indirectly and does not itself render anything.

A React UI component that renders a sortable, filterable table of flamegraph data (service/operation, count, self, total) inside the Trace Flamegraph view. It takes a props contract and emits a row-click event, so it is a reusable component definition. It is a notable UI part of the flamegraph feature, not a routable view.

An inline arrow-function property in the default config. It only opens a documentation URL in a new window. This is a trivial UI callback below the granularity of an architectural element, with no callers and no meaningful behaviour of its own.

BreakableText is a small reusable React presentational component that splits text into spans so that long words can wrap. It is used by a couple of other components. It is a minor UI library primitive with a props interface but little architectural weight, so it gets low significance.

Type-only module declaring prop and row shapes for the DetailsCard UI component. These are supporting TypeScript type aliases (column defs, styled values, filter dropdown props) with no behaviour. They are an implementation detail of the component rather than an architectural element on their own.

A React UI component that renders a settings dropdown menu for toggling the timeline, heatmap and side panel in the trace page header. It is a reusable component with a props contract, used by TracePageHeader. It renders UI but does not emit telemetry itself, so it is a notable UX element rather than an APM element.

Module declaring the ITableSpan interface, an in-code data structure that carries aggregated span statistics rows for the Trace Statistics table. It is not persisted and not published as a schema, so it is an application data object of minor, local significance.

A trivial store action that only forwards its payload to viewModifierRemoval in the DeepDependencies client-side state store. It is a one-line delegation with no logic of its own, an implementation detail below the granularity an architecture model would record.

React component module rendering the flamegraph's right-click context menu. It accepts props and emits callbacks for reset, collapse, copy and highlight actions. It is a reusable UI component within the trace flamegraph view, a notable but local UI unit rather than a routable view.

Inline mouse-move handler inside the assistant panel's resize logic; computes a drag delta and sets the clamped panel width. It is a trivial UI implementation detail, not a named architectural element, though it does drive user-facing UI behaviour.

Utility module of small value formatters (date ISO conversion, padding, numeric offset) used for link pattern parameter substitution. It is a formatting helper, below the granularity of an architecture element. Its console.error calls are incidental diagnostics, not telemetry.

An ambient TypeScript declaration file that supplies type shims for third-party modules (logfmt, store, d3-flame-graph). It is build-time typing boilerplate with no runtime behaviour, so it is not an architectural element.

A one-line entry in a Redux action-to-analytics-tracker map that delegates to trackDetailState with trackTags. It is a trivial wiring lambda with no logic of its own, below the granularity a maintainer would name. The analytics tracking work happens in the callee, not here.
